title: Dual-Hemispheric Whole-Brain Battery Series (DHB-1 through DHB-3R) — Finding the Last Invisible Class, Two Repairs, and the Convergence Floor Priced as One Number
description:
The complete dual-hemispheric testing arc of October 13, 2026, published as one record: three attack batteries, two repairs deployed through the human-approved self-improvement cycle, and one convergence battery that prices the whole system's final floor as a single number. Every battery was preregistered (committed to git) before execution; every instrument defect was disclosed in the receipts rather than patched; every repair carries a conforming-identity receipt proving the deployed change left legitimate behavior byte-identical.

Sequence, as run:

DHB-1 (finding). Conforming out-of-profile inputs break the bounded rule: unbounded negative runaway, weight driven to -21.88, 598 healing decisions lost. The left hemisphere (governance) and the fail-safe direction held — the attack moved the dial, never the rules. Two instrument defects disclosed in the receipt.

SIP-5 (repair, human-approved). Profile-tight domains plus a confidence clamp plus a nightly tripwire. Conforming-identity receipt: byte-identical on the frozen corpus. DHB-1R: all seven falsifiers pass — boundedness restored, decision identity exact.

DHB-2 (finding). Fully-conforming, in-profile, registry-valid issuer traffic is invisible to every deployed layer while steering the whole brain's disposition: 60/60 forged records accepted, attributed as legitimate drift, flagged by nothing. Fail-safe held again (the dial, never the rules). The crossing had no provenance.

SIP-6 (repair, human-approved). The signed issuance registry — HMAC-SHA256 over the issued-id block, key in process custody, registry anchored in git and re-read from git objects at verification time, fail-closed (an unverifiable registry means nothing is issued). The data-plane mirror of the earlier governance-side signed-release defense. DHB-2R: all falsifiers pass — the campaign flips from invisible to detected, 60/60 held as unsigned_issuance, steering collapses to zero, conforming identity byte-identical.

DHB-3 (the convergence battery). Keys plus commit access on both planes simultaneously: every local software layer falls, as predicted. The clamp alone holds boundedness even under total governance compromise — 9600 decision events against 2646 in clean operation: sick, but honest and contained. The final floor priced as one number: zero machine-checkable external anchors.

SIP-7 (repair, human-approved). Anchor binding: the three anchor fingerprints (signed issuance registry, governance release registry, signing key pin) are DOI-bound in this record; an external verification leg in the run-end audit compares live anchor shas against the published record; fail-closed handling if the binding is unverifiable.

DHB-3R. The one number is 1, ENFORCED: the external check detects both forged registries without trusting local git. The maximal attacker must additionally defeat Zenodo itself — the honest regress floor, stated as found.

Guard evolution shipped inline: ingestion guard v2.1 to v2.3 (format registry and full-field numeric validation; profile-tight domains and confidence clamp; signed issuance registry), with conforming-identity receipts for each deployment. All data is synthetic; no real customer or production system is involved at any point.

Dual Mesh Benchmark: MEASURED (DeepSeek column, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241); all other figures NOT MEASURED.

This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All data is synthetic.
